tool_arguments.query: Marvell Technology data-center revenue Q3 fiscal 2027 custom AI silicon electro-optics

events.content: Marvell Technology data-center revenue Q3 fiscal 2027 custom AI silicon electro-optics

Marvell had **not yet reported Q3 fiscal 2027 data-center revenue** as of its latest reported quarter; Q2 FY2027 ended August 1, 2026, and data-center revenue was **$2.172 billion**, up **46% year over year** and **18% sequentially**, representing **79%** of total revenue. [[1]] 

For Q3 FY2027, Marvell guided total company revenue to roughly **$3.15 billion** (±5%), while an industry analysis estimated data-center revenue would rise about **20% sequentially** and **75% year over year**; applying 20% to Q2’s $2.172 billion implies approximately **$2.61 billion** in Q3 data-center revenue. [[2]] [[1]] 

The expected Q3 step-up reflects broad data-center demand, with management specifically citing strong connectivity demand and a **significant acceleration in Custom silicon beginning in the second half of FY2027**. [[1]] 

Marvell does **not** disclose quarterly revenue separately for custom AI silicon versus electro-optics in its reported end-market table; however, its FY2026 investor materials characterize optical interconnect as roughly **half of data-center revenue** and custom silicon as approximately **25%** of data-center revenue. [[3]] 

A third-party model estimated Q2 FY2027 electro-optical-component revenue at approximately **$1.4 billion**, up **97.2% year over year**, indicating that optics remained the larger near-term AI revenue contributor even as custom silicon began to accelerate. [[2]] 

The relevant product set includes 800G and 1.6T scale-out optics, NPO/CPO scale-up optical solutions, data-center interconnect modules, and custom XPU/XPU-attach solutions. [[4]]

tool_arguments.query: Marvell Technology FY2026 custom AI silicon revenue percentage data-center

events.content: Marvell Technology FY2026 custom AI silicon revenue percentage data-center

**Marvell Technology — Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended August 2, 2025):** total revenue reached a record **$2.006 billion**, up **58% year over year** and **6% sequentially**; GAAP diluted EPS was **$0.22** and non-GAAP diluted EPS was **$0.67**. [[1]]

**Data center was the core growth engine:** revenue was **$1.491 billion**, representing **74% of company revenue**, up **69% year over year** and **3% sequentially** from $1.441 billion in Q1 FY2026. [[2]]

**Custom AI silicon and electro-optics:** management identified strong AI demand for these two product categories as a principal driver of the quarter’s growth, and stated that custom-AI design activity had reached an all-time high, with **more than 50 new opportunities across more than 10 customers**. [[2, 3]] 

Marvell did **not** disclose separate Q2 revenue amounts for custom AI silicon versus electro-optics; rather, it stated on the earnings call that the two product lines together accounted for **more than three quarters of data-center revenue**, implying more than roughly **$1.1 billion** of the $1.491 billion data-center total. [[4, 2]] 

For Q3 FY2026, Marvell guided total revenue to **$2.060 billion ±5%**; management expected overall data-center revenue to be approximately flat sequentially, as electro-optics strength offsets a near-term decline in custom revenue, while expecting custom-business growth to become substantially stronger in Q4. [[2, 4]]

**Bottom line:** Q2 demonstrated that Marvell’s AI exposure is already highly material—data center supplied nearly three quarters of revenue and its custom/optical franchises comprised the majority of that segment—but the Q3 outlook also illustrates that custom-silicon ramps can be nonlinear and customer-program timing can create quarterly volatility. [[2, 4]]

private_messages.content:
**Marvell Technology — Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended August 2, 2025):** total revenue reached a record **$2.006 billion**, up **58% year over year** and **6% sequentially**; GAAP diluted EPS was **$0.22** and non-GAAP diluted EPS was **$0.67**. [[1]]

**Data center was the core growth engine:** revenue was **$1.491 billion**, representing **74% of company revenue**, up **69% year over year** and **3% sequentially** from $1.441 billion in Q1 FY2026. [[2]]

**Custom AI silicon and electro-optics:** management identified strong AI demand for these two product categories as a principal driver of the quarter’s growth, and stated that custom-AI design activity had reached an all-time high, with **more than 50 new opportunities across more than 10 customers**. [[2, 3]] 

Marvell did **not** disclose separate Q2 revenue amounts for custom AI silicon versus electro-optics; rather, it stated on the earnings call that the two product lines together accounted for **more than three quarters of data-center revenue**, implying more than roughly **$1.1 billion** of the $1.491 billion data-center total. [[4, 2]] 

For Q3 FY2026, Marvell guided total revenue to **$2.060 billion ±5%**; management expected overall data-center revenue to be approximately flat sequentially, as electro-optics strength offsets a near-term decline in custom revenue, while expecting custom-business growth to become substantially stronger in Q4. [[2, 4]]

**Bottom line:** Q2 demonstrated that Marvell’s AI exposure is already highly material—data center supplied nearly three quarters of revenue and its custom/optical franchises comprised the majority of that segment—but the Q3 outlook also illustrates that custom-silicon ramps can be nonlinear and customer-program timing can create quarterly volatility. [[2, 4]]
